d5e34ba54f56b89718b2c6e849407bb3dedf3f8d.summary: Dutch national police (Politie) news item, published 13 November 2025, reporting that Operation Endgame disrupted the infostealer Rhadamanthys, the remote access trojan VenomRAT and the Elysium botnet. The police say these malware types infected hundreds of thousands of victims worldwide. They describe Operation Endgame as started in 2022 and as the largest international operation against ransomware and cybercrime.

d575a6482d9b8e691b7033592928e91ae53c2aa1.summary: InQuest's blog describes a holiday-season Dridex campaign that delivers malware through password-protected Microsoft Excel spreadsheets with macros. Lures included a CDC COVID-19 form, a fake resume, fake spreadsheets, and emails posing as office memos and vaccination rules that carried the spreadsheet passwords. Once opened, the macro calls an embedded script that fetches further payloads, which are distributed via Discord CDN servers. The report withholds payload URI patterns and expects Dridex to become more elusive over time.

d550bcfc9e48736defc43baa88cd510cd28b1aba.summary: FortiGuard Labs describes C0XMO, a new Gafgyt-derived botnet variant for Linux and IoT devices. It spreads by exploiting CVE-2021-27137 in the UPnP service of DD-WRT router firmware. A separate Python scanner brute-forces Telnet and SSH logins and runs HTTP exploits, including CVE-2015-2051, CVE-2022-35914, and CVE-2025-34054, to deploy bots. The malware sets up persistence with cron jobs and shell profiles, removes rival botnets, and supports 19 DDoS attack methods. The report says its design suggests more operational sophistication than typical Gafgyt malware.
